neighbours.label: the determiner or number right after 'journal X published / contains / features', where a paper, article or study is about to be named; journal mentions without that slot, and other publishers, are quiet
fire: The June issue of the Journal of Marine Biology contains five articles on deep-sea corals.
Earlier this month Nature published three studies on the origin of the virus.
In its spring issue, the journal Neuron features two reports on memory in mice.
In 1998 the journal Econometrica published a long paper on auction design.
The latest issue of the British Medical Journal includes four papers on vaccine safety.
This week The Lancet published two articles about malaria in children.
The current volume of the Journal of Applied Physics carries six papers on thin films.
Last year the journal Icarus published a short study of the rings of Saturn.
quiet: The June menu of the harbour restaurant contains five dishes made with fresh crab.
Earlier this month the tabloid printed three photos of the singer's wedding.
The journal Neuron was founded in 1988 and is edited in Cambridge.
In 1998 the brewery released a dark ale with a bitter finish.
The offices of the British Medical Journal are a short walk from the station.
This week the gallery displayed two portraits of children by the painter.
The current catalogue of the hardware shop lists six kinds of hammer.
Last year the label released a short album of piano pieces.

notes: Card: peaks on ' this', ' a', ' two', ' three', ' classic' before paper/article/issue; output promotes ' studies', ' article', ' papers', ' paper'. Probes: 'contains four articles' 1.01, 'features three reports' 1.11, 'Science published two studies' 0.67, 'Nature published a short paper' 0.49; 'newspaper published a photo' 0.03, 'journal Nature is based in London' 0.04, 'second of three papers' 0.04.
